questions: Does the five-sensor spacing of 0.02 m give a smooth signal, or do readings jump between sensors at the edges?
Does the 0.05 m sensor lead cause lag or overshoot on tight bends? If so, would reducing it to 0.03 m help?
Is wheel_track 0.12 m with wheel_radius 0.03 m giving enough turn authority for the slalom?
Is any of the geometry being bounded by the limits in a way that limits your controller?

intent: Baseline five-sensor array, evenly spaced 0.02 m across the line, 0.05 m ahead of the axle, with a 12 mm footprint. Moderate track, wheel radius and mass for stable, responsive turning. Purpose: establish a clean baseline and measure how the sensor lead and spacing affect line tracking on the development tracks. Expected: completion on the oval and s-bend, with the slalom as the hardest case.
learning: Iteration 0 is a baseline with no race evidence. Next, adjust sensor lead and spacing based on the race's rms_error and max_error on the slalom and s-bend, and on steering_oscillation as a sign of lag from the sensor lead.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or Integrator feedback yet. The public contract gives the geometry levers that matter. The off-track limit is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4). With a 12.5 mm tape half-width, body widths up to about 0.18 m still resolve to 0.06 m, so body width is nearly free and I keep it moderate at 0.10 m. A 12 mm sensor footprint on a 25 mm tape can read a full-tape value over a wide band of offsets, while still giving a graded reading at the edges. I place five sensors across x = -0.04 to +0.04 at 0.02 m spacing. That covers the tape at the robot's centre and at moderate lateral error, and gives the weighted signal a usable range. The sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle so the robot sees the line before it reaches the wheels, which should reduce oscillation on bends. The wheel track of 0.12 m and wheel radius of 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate per PWM difference. Mass of 0.8 kg and body length of 0.16 m keep yaw inertia moderate, so the robot can turn without excessive overshoot. Expected result: a first completed run on the oval with a small RMS error. The main risk is that the 0.05 m sensor lead lets the signal lag on tight bends, so I ask for line-loss and oscillation data to test that.
